gloss: to order; to place an order; to request

definitions.gloss: to order; to place an order (for goods, food, services)
definitions.explanation: To request the purchase or preparation of goods, food, or services. The most common everyday meaning.

definitions.gloss: to make demands; to impose conditions; to make requests
definitions.explanation: To specify requirements or make particular demands. Often implies being particular or picky about how something should be done.

examples.japanese: コーヒーを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
ネットで{本|ほん}を{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
{料理|りょうり}を{注文|ちゅうもん}してから{届|とど}くまで30{分|ぷん}もかかった。
examples.english: It took 30 minutes from when I ordered the food to when it arrived.

examples.japanese: {注文|ちゅうもん}が{多|おお}い{客|きゃく}だ。
{監督|かんとく}は{選手|せんしゅ}に{細|こま}かい{注文|ちゅうもん}をつけた。
examples.english: The coach made detailed demands of the players.

examples.japanese: デザインに{注文|ちゅうもん}をつけすぎると、かえって{仕上|しあ}がりが{悪|わる}くなることがある。
examples.english: If you make too many demands about the design, the final result can actually turn out worse.

notes:
One of the most essential words for daily life in Japan — used at restaurants, shops, and online. The noun {注文|ちゅうもん} is extremely common on its own. Sense 2 uses the expression {注文|ちゅうもん}をつける (to attach demands/conditions).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {注文|ちゅうもん}を{受|う}ける: to take an order
- {注文|ちゅうもん}{品|ひん}: ordered item
- {注文|ちゅうもん}{番号|ばんごう}: order number
- {注文|ちゅうもん}をつける: to make demands, to specify conditions
- {特別|とくべつ}{注文|ちゅうもん}: special order, custom order

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {発注|はっちゅう}する: to place an order — business/commercial context, for placing orders with suppliers
- {頼|たの}む: to order; to ask — more casual (used at restaurants informally)
- オーダーする: to order — English loanword, common in fashion and food service
